result.report:
The supplied argument establishes the stated partial theorem for each prescribed rational-coefficient reference, in the declared real scalar extension on finite rational spatial domains. The arbitrary balanced-space P05.2 classification and the negative assertion for every real-coefficient reference remain open. Neither is needed for this verdict.

I checked the definitions and comparison-proof boundaries against the authentic [BMPS v1 manuscript](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1), using identified statements rather than trusting cached line ranges. Its literal coefficient restrictions are explicitly replaced here. The substantive dependency chain is reconstructed in the supplied argument; no external theorem, predecessor verdict, computation, or compilation result is essential.

The elementary polyhedral arguments suffice for the required cone generators, vertex/recession decompositions, projections, separations, and supergradient calculations. The graph kernel argument is valid: a second kernel direction would permit a nonproportional positive perturbation of the actual weights, contradicting (1). Consequently each vertex has a primitive positive integer relation. Weight ratios propagate consistently around cycles, leaving one arbitrary positive real scale per connected component. Bivalent propagation identifies every unbranched component with a complete rational affine line; this preserves its carrier and actual weight, with original subdivisions recoverable by refinement.

The intersection reconstruction retains saturated lattices. For a two-cone generated by primitive rays r,s, the representative s/χ differs from an integral primitive quotient lift only tangentially. Formula (5) cancels that discrepancy. The refinement cases establish compatibility at both recursive stages, including zero coefficients at newly inserted vertices. Formula (6) establishes first-divisor balancing. Commutativity also follows directly: the mixed coefficient is Σ_C(ω_C/χ_C)[h(s)g(r)+h(r)g(s)]−Σ_r t_r h(r)g(r), which is symmetric. Locality and annihilation of ambient affine functions follow from (5). The PC-to-PAPC construction uses genuine rational endpoints and then rational generators of the nonnegative balancing cone; it therefore covers every nonnegative real local cycle on every ordinary open, including nonproduct one-cycles. Only dimensions one and two occur on this carrier.

For the positive direction, the scalar completion lemma correctly forces endpoint continuity and finite outgoing derivatives through the positive vertex PCC. Its converse handles arbitrary cofaces, remote endpoints, real coefficients, and real centres: convex graph projections lie in straight chains, while branched-centre displacements satisfy (9). The partial infimum of a raw competitor satisfies the rational graph inequalities, and finiteness propagates through every connected component. No continuity assumption on raw competitors is required.

The interval D includes all vertical recession constraints and is compact with zero in its interior. Fibre minimization is justified by pointedness and nonnegative recession objective. The trace representation (14) retains endpoint fibres, and the tail slopes retain mixed recession behaviour. The incidence system includes every bounded edge and cycle. Its feasible witness, closure under coordinatewise maxima, and compact maximization establish the greatest assignment. Elimination gives the finite affine minima (17) with rational p-gradients despite real constants.

The supremum (18) establishes the full cylinder envelope for nonseparable data. Each fixed-p function is actual PC, so their supremum satisfies every PCC. Touching supports of rational vertical slices bound every raw competitor at rational points; small same-face rational simplices extend this bound to every real centre. The explicit lower competitor γ−||u||∞ supplies two-sided growth. This proves raw equality, rather than merely constructing a scalar incidence solution. Chamber-endpoint maximization produces jointly convex affine maxima on each strip; it does not assume bilinear interpolation is convex.

The rational-domain gate is established independently of the possibly real chamber endpoints. In (21)–(22), spatial vertices and rays come from rational supergradient endpoints, rational primitive lengths, and rational normal generators. These domains glue at graph nodes and have no vertices in open bounded strips or distant tails. Original subdivisions introduce no additional measure coefficients by refinement compatibility. Thus rectangle interiors, edge fibres, all ends, and all junction fibres are accounted for.

The contact proof covers both exposed-slope cases. A singleton C_x produces a germ affine in the vertical direction and zero second coefficient. For a nondegenerate C_x, (26) makes the fibre minimization coercive. A noncontact point forces strict caps for interior p, and greatest-assignment maximality forces the vertex Laplacian to vanish. Positive weights and concavity then force every outgoing slope function to be affine on C_x. The rank-one relation produces the ambient forms in (27), with rational B. After affine subtraction, the first divisor is supported where the residual function vanishes, so its entire second divisor is zero. This proves contact at every possible noncontact atom. Finite components and their actual positive product scales preserve the conclusion. The same rational-domain argument validates the separately stated positive strengthening to real-coefficient references on rational domains.

For the negative direction, (29)–(31) establish global coercivity on every reference cell and component, including bounded cells and all recession directions. The rational maps (32) factor through the full direction kernels without replacing the actual lattices. The choices of ε and C make P=max(γ,εH+C) rational-domain actual PC and equal to the unchanged prescribed γ outside a compact set. The obstacle (37) is nonnegative, bounded, compactly supported, and rational-PA. The endpoints (36) form an actual original-product PCC and have P=C and zero bump, forcing the raw value at o to be at most P(o). All other structure vertices have zero bump. The far-rational-endpoint argument (38), using only upper growth, establishes q≤P on every cell at every real centre. Hence (39) is exact globally, including cycles, ends, and other components.

The complete junction recursion checks out. The saturated product plane lattice gives the primitive kink vector (41) and indices Q/g and P/g. The kink weights are 2c_kΩ_ij g/D; the axis weights are abλ_i(4−2c_k) and abμ_j(4−2c_l). Kink values vanish in the second recursion, while the two complete axis sums contribute 4ab each. Thus the junction coefficient is 8ε²ab, with no division by 2!. The bump is one at o and zero at every other P-structure vertex. Obstacle refinements add only zero second coefficients. Therefore the whole integral, including every other gap term, is exactly −8ε²ab.

Both envelopes are actual PAPC functions in the fixed growth class. The explicit sequence P+1/n decreases uniformly and has identical recursive measures, establishing regularization and the operator domain without an imported extension theorem or an escaping-mass argument.

One harmless correction is needed: the reference to the tangential correction “in (36)” preceding (45) should refer to (5)–(6), together with (44). The displayed arithmetic is correct. No substantial repair is required.
